question:
A student uses classical wave theory to argue that when a very weak light beam of intensity $I$ falls on a metal surface, an electron should require an appreciable time to absorb enough energy to escape, because the absorbed energy should build up gradually with exposure time.

In an experiment, however, photoelectrons are observed to be emitted with essentially zero time lag (emission time $<10^{-9}\,\text{s}$) even when the intensity is very low.

Critically evaluate what this observation implies about the mechanism of energy transfer from light to electrons. Based on this evaluation, state what must be true about the nature of energy absorption in the photoelectric effect.

options.A: Electrons slowly store wave energy for long durations and then release it instantaneously once a threshold is reached
options.B: The metal surface behaves like a capacitor that accumulates energy before releasing electrons suddenly
options.C: Energy transfer does not occur continuously; it occurs in discrete packets (quanta) that are absorbed in a single event by an electron
options.D: The speed of light becomes infinite at microscopic scales, causing instantaneous emission
